hostos.oneLineEn: Puerto Rican educator-ethicist linking social ethics and Antillean liberation to positivism and anti-colonialism.

hu-yuan.oneLineEn: Northern Song educator-Confucian known for the Anding school and classics-plus-affairs pedagogy.

huan-tan.oneLineEn: Han-Xin transitional thinker known for New Discourses and anti-omen-lore stance.

hui-shi.oneLineEn: Warring States School of Names figure with Zhuangzi, known for disputation and uniting same-different.

ibn-bajja.oneLineEn: Andalusian philosopher who, in Governance of the Solitary, asked how sages keep perfection in imperfect cities.

ibn-gabirol.oneLineEn: In Fons Vitae set out Neoplatonic metaphysics; known in Latin scholasticism as Avicebron.

ibn-hazm.oneLineEn: Andalusian Ẓāhirī thinker combining law, logic, religious polemic, and love literature.

ibn-taymiyya.oneLineEn: Ḥanbalī jurist-critic opposing philosophy, kalām, and Sufi monism; shaped later political theology.

ibn-tufayl.oneLineEn: Andalusian author of Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān, in which island reason rises from nature to metaphysics and religion.

ignacio-ellacuria.oneLineEn: Salvadoran Jesuit whose historical reality joined liberation philosophy, theology, and politics.

isaac-israeli.oneLineEn: Early medieval Jewish Neoplatonist linking Arabic philosophy to Jewish thought.

isaac-luria.oneLineEn: Core Lurianic Kabbalist remaking early modern Jewish mysticism via contraction, shattering, and repair.

ito-jinsai.oneLineEn: Edo Ancient Learning figure who returned to Confucius-Mencius texts and criticized Zhu Xi learning.

ivan-kireevsky.oneLineEn: Co-founder of Slavophilism; integral knowledge and Orthodoxy against West European rationalism.

jacques-maritain.oneLineEn: Neo-Thomism and human-rights philosophy; fills modern Catholic political philosophy.

jaimini.oneLineEn: Traditional author of the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra; identity-tier anchor of early Mīmāṃsā ritual hermeneutics.

jamgon-kongtrul.oneLineEn: Rimé core figure integrating multiple Tibetan traditions in the Treasury of Knowledge and Five Treasuries.

jan-patocka.oneLineEn: Czech phenomenology and dissident political thought; fills Husserl-Heidegger Eastern European lines.

jane-addams.oneLineEn: Social ethics, democracy, and pragmatist reform; fills American women's philosophy.

jankelevitch.oneLineEn: The ineffable and the unforgivable in morals; after Bergson.
